claims.statement: Rule set v18 passed pre-release testing against 14 days of historical orders with no defect found in the allocation logic; however, the replay testing explicitly did not exercise carrier scheduling
claims.corroboration: Tier-1 verified replay results from Inventory Control; explicit acknowledgment that carrier scheduling was not tested
claims.limitation: The rule logic is correct, but the interaction between split-reservation and carrier scheduling was not validated pre-release

claims.statement: The combination of: (1) all 186 held orders being v18-affected EXC-0921, (2) v18 logic passing testing but carrier scheduling not exercised, and (3) Carrier Ops stating corrections must follow lag identification, points to a carrier-scheduling interaction issue rather than a pure allocation logic defect
claims.corroboration: Three distinct tier-1 sources (Inventory Control twice, Carrier Ops) converge on this pattern
claims.limitation: This is inference; requires discriminating evidence from deeper investigation of the handoff or dock interactions

capability_gaps.reason: Need to understand the exact state transitions and handoff points where EXC-0921 orders interact with the carrier scheduling system; this will identify whether the bottleneck is in allocation-to-carrier-feed handoff, dock assignment, or carrier-side lag

next_action.rationale: C8 establishes that carrier scheduling was untested in v18 regression. C9 infers that the issue is at the intersection of v18 split-reservation and carrier scheduling. Tracing the cohort handoffs will show precisely where EXC-0921 orders stall and with what system they interact at that point.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Reveal whether the bottleneck is: (a) the allocation-to-carrier-feed transition, (b) dock capacity/assignment logic, or (c) confirmed carrier-side lag; this will discriminate whether reverting v18 or correcting slots is the appropriate mitigation
